title: The Bank Nobody Could Kill: Basel's Reparations Machine Outlives Its Mandate and Captures Its Founders

extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: The Hague Agreements of January 1930 chartered the BIS to collect and administer Germany's Young Plan reparation payments — a perpetual toll on a sovereign's output, extracted via intergovernmental debt schedules inherited from the Dawes Plan.
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: The victors' central banks seated the institution in Basel, outside any single nation's jurisdiction, with constituent charters granting legal immunity to its assets and archives — an extraction instrument built constitutionally beyond audit, seizure, or subpoena.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: Charter-level archive immunity meant the BIS's ledgers were closed to national parliaments and courts; during WWII it operated gold and foreign-exchange channels with all belligerents while its American president Thomas H. McKittrick kept lines open to both Allied and Axis central banks, all under diplomatic darkness.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: After the Hoover Moratorium (1931) and Lausanne (1932) killed the reparations flow it existed to manage, the BIS did not dissolve — it repurposed into the monopoly clearinghouse and club of central bankers, a wartime intermediary whose neutrality charter was itself the market.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: The March 1939 Czech gold affair — transfer of Czechoslovak National Bank gold to the Reichsbank after the German occupation of Prague — scandalised Westminster, yet no charter was revoked; Bretton Woods (July 1944) resolved the BIS should be liquidated 'at the earliest possible moment,' and the 1948 post-war settlement quietly let it stand.

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: It inherited the Dawes Plan machinery and the victors' central-bank cartel of the 1920s, hardening the Young Plan's reparations administration into a treaty-chartered institution with sovereign immunity.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: It created the permanent unelected central bankers' club in Basel — the model for post-war machinery including the Basel Committee on bank capital standards, drafted outside any democratic legislature.
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: Reparations revenue died in 1932, but the immunity and neutrality frameworks kept the BIS earning on gold and exchange operations for all belligerents throughout WWII, recycling crisis into institutional endowment and insider standing.
closedLoopRatchet.enablesNextDossier: Its survival past Bretton Woods's liquidation resolution established that crisis machinery outlives its mandate — the operating template for the offshore black-ledger and capital-standards architecture that governs sovereign and bank debt ever since.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: The BIS was Hitler's bank — a Nazi plot from the start.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: It was designed by the victors' central bankers under the Young Plan committee in January 1930, before Hitler took power; its wartime service to all belligerents flowed from the immunity and neutrality written into its 1930 charters, not from any Nazi origin.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: The institution's documented purpose was debt collection on Germany; its acceptance of Czechoslovak National Bank gold for the Reichsbank in March 1939, its survival past the death of reparations in 1932, and its defiance of Bretton Woods's 1944 liquidation resolution show how crisis machinery outlives its mandate and captures its founders.
